facts.fact_text: The applicants in all three applications (nos. 69483/13, 76319/13, and 30456/14) were members of a political group called the Public Chamber (İctimai Palata).
As members of the Public Chamber (İctimai Palata), the applicants planned to hold several assemblies in 2012 in Baku.
The applicants in application no. 69483/13 planned an assembly in the form of a picketing, to be held on 22 April 2012.
The applicants in application no. 69483/13 gave a notice to the Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) in advance of the planned assembly.

According to the notice given to the Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA), the assembly planned by the applicants in application no. 69483/13 was scheduled to take place from 12 p.m. to 1 p.m. on 22 April 2012.

According to the notice given to the Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA), the assembly planned by the applicants in application no. 69483/13 was scheduled to take place in front of the Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) building.
According to the notice given to the Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA), the expected participation in the assembly planned by the applicants in application no. 69483/13 was fifty individuals.
The purpose of the assembly planned by the applicants in application no. 69483/13 was to demand the removal of unwritten restrictions placed on the freedom of assembly.
The purpose of the assembly planned by the applicants in application no. 69483/13 was to demand political reforms.
The purpose of the assembly planned by the applicants in application no. 69483/13 was to demand freedom for political prisoners.
The assembly planned by the applicants in application no. 69483/13 was not eventually held.
The applicants in application no. 76319/13 planned an assembly in the form of a march followed by a meeting, to be held on 22 April 2012.
The applicants in application no. 76319/13 gave a notice to the Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) in advance of the planned assembly.

According to the notice given to the Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA), the assembly planned by the applicants in application no. 76319/13 was scheduled to take place from 4 p.m. to 6 p.m. on 22 April 2012.
According to the notice given to the Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA), the expected participation in the assembly planned by the applicants in application no. 76319/13 was ten thousand people.
The applicants in application no. 76319/13 proposed a location in the Nizami district of Baku, namely a square in front of the Tabriz cinema, for the holding of the assembly.
The applicants in application no. 76319/13 proposed a location in the Binagadi district of Baku for the holding of the assembly.
The applicants in application no. 76319/13 proposed a location in the Narimanov district of Baku for the holding of the assembly.
The applicants in application no. 76319/13 asked the Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) to agree to one of the three proposed locations for the assembly.
According to the content of the slogans to be used, the purpose of the assembly planned by the applicants in application no. 76319/13 included demanding new parliamentary elections.
According to the content of the slogans to be used, the purpose of the assembly planned by the applicants in application no. 76319/13 included demanding political reforms.
According to the content of the slogans to be used, the purpose of the assembly planned by the applicants in application no. 76319/13 included demanding freedom for political prisoners.

According to the content of the slogans to be used, the purpose of the assembly planned by the applicants in application no. 76319/13 included demanding protection of the right to freedom of assembly.
According to the content of the slogans to be used, the purpose of the assembly planned by the applicants in application no. 76319/13 included protesting against corruption.
According to the content of the slogans to be used, the purpose of the assembly planned by the applicants in application no. 76319/13 included protesting against violation of property rights.

By a letter of 18 April 2012, the Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) refused to authorise the assembly planned by the applicants in application no. 76319/13 at any of the three locations proposed by the applicants.

The Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA), in its letter of 18 April 2012, proposed another location for the assembly planned by the applicants in application no. 76319/13, namely the grounds of a driving school situated in the 20th residential area of the Sabail district, on the outskirts of Baku.

The Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) noted in its letter of 18 April 2012 that the locations indicated by the applicants in application no. 76319/13 were 'areas with intense traffic, and therefore it was not possible to hold assemblies there'.

The Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) noted in its letter of 18 April 2012 that 'it was not possible to ensure security in respect of the assembly planned by the applicants in application no. 76319/13, considering the serious problems that the assembly would cause to the free movement of citizens who did not want to participate in it, and to the smooth functioning of transport'.

Following the refusal of the authorisation, the applicants in application no. 76319/13 decided to hold the assembly at the place proposed by the Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA), namely the grounds of a driving school situated in the 20th residential area of the Sabail district.
The applicant in application no. 30456/14 planned an assembly in the form of a march, to be held on 13 October 2012.
The applicant in application no. 30456/14 gave a notice to the Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) in advance of the planned assembly.

According to the notice given to the Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA), the assembly planned by the applicant in application no. 30456/14 was scheduled to take place from 4 p.m. to 6 p.m. on 13 October 2012.
According to the notice given to the Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA), the expected participation in the assembly planned by the applicant in application no. 30456/14 was ten thousand people.

According to the notice given to the Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA), the march planned by the applicant in application no. 30456/14 was to start at a square adjacent to the Parliament Avenue in Baku.
According to the notice given to the Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA), the march planned by the applicant in application no. 30456/14 was to follow Parliament Avenue in Baku.
According to the notice given to the Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA), the march planned by the applicant in application no. 30456/14 was to finish in front of the Parliament building in Baku.
The purpose of the assembly planned by the applicant in application no. 30456/14 was to demand early elections to the Parliament of Azerbaijan.
By a letter of 18 April 2012, the Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) refused to authorise the assembly planned by the applicants in application no. 69483/13.

The Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) stated in its letter of 18 April 2012 that the assembly proposed by the applicants in application no. 69483/13 was 'to no purpose' (keçirilməsi məqsədəuyğun hesab olunmur) because another assembly with a similar cause had already been designated a location on the same day.

By a letter of 18 April 2012, the Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) refused to authorise the assembly planned by the applicants in application no. 76319/13 at any of the three locations proposed by the applicants.

The Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) noted in its letter of 18 April 2012 that 'it was not possible to ensure security in respect of the assembly planned by the applicants in application no. 76319/13, considering the serious problems that the assembly would cause to the free movement of citizens who did not want to participate in it, and to the smooth functioning of transport'.

By a letter of 10 October 2012, the Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) refused to authorise the assembly planned by the applicant in application no. 30456/14 at the location indicated by the applicant.

The Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA), in its letter of 10 October 2012, proposed another location for the assembly planned by the applicant in application no. 30456/14, namely the grounds of a driving school situated in the 20th residential area of the Sabail district, on the outskirts of Baku — the same location proposed by the Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) in application no. 76319/13.

The Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) noted in its letter of 10 October 2012 that the location indicated by the applicant in application no. 30456/14 was an 'area with intense traffic, and therefore it was not possible to hold assemblies there'.

The Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) noted in its letter of 10 October 2012 that 'it was not possible to ensure security in respect of the assembly planned by the applicant in application no. 30456/14, considering the serious problems that the assembly would cause to the free movement of citizens who did not want to participate in it, and to the smooth functioning of transport'.

Having received the refusal letters from the Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA), the applicants lodged complaints in the form of a civil action against the Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) before the Baku Administrative Economic Court No. 1.
In their complaints before the Baku Administrative Economic Court No. 1, the applicants argued that their right to freedom of assembly had been violated.

In all three applications (nos. 69483/13, 76319/13, and 30456/14), the applicants asked the Baku Administrative Economic Court No. 1 to declare the Baku City Executive Authority's (BCEA's) decisions unlawful.
In application no. 30456/14, the applicant asked the Baku Administrative Economic Court No. 1 to order the Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) to authorise the assembly.
In applications nos. 69483/13 and 76319/13, the applicants asked the Baku Administrative Economic Court No. 1 to order the Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) to pay non-pecuniary damages.
In each of the three cases, the applicants challenged the lawfulness of the Baku City Executive Authority's (BCEA's) decisions before the Baku Administrative Economic Court No. 1.
In each of the three cases, the applicants challenged the proportionality of the Baku City Executive Authority's (BCEA's) decisions before the Baku Administrative Economic Court No. 1.

The applicants in application no. 69483/13 argued before the Baku Administrative Economic Court No. 1 that it had been unlawful to refuse the authorisation of their assembly simply because another assembly with similar slogans had been planned elsewhere in Baku on the same date.

The applicants in application no. 76319/13 argued before the Baku Administrative Economic Court No. 1 that one of the locations they had proposed — namely, a square in front of the Tabriz cinema in the Nizami district of Baku — was on the Baku City Executive Authority's (BCEA's) indicative list of places for the holding of public assemblies.

The Baku City Executive Authority's (BCEA's) indicative list of places for the holding of public assemblies had been prepared in accordance with Article 9 § VI of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998.
The Baku City Executive Authority's (BCEA's) indicative list of places for the holding of public assemblies was published in the Official Gazette, Azerbaijan newspaper.

The applicants in application no. 76319/13 submitted a copy of the Baku City Executive Authority's (BCEA's) indicative list of places for the holding of public assemblies to the domestic courts, but not to the Court.

The applicant in application no. 30456/14 argued before the Baku Administrative Economic Court No. 1 that the Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) had failed to present any evidence in support of its allegations.

The applicants in application no. 76319/13 argued before the Baku Administrative Economic Court No. 1 that the location on the outskirts of Baku proposed by the Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) — namely, the grounds of a driving school situated in the 20th residential area of the Sabail district — was unfit for holding public assemblies.

The applicant in application no. 30456/14 argued before the Baku Administrative Economic Court No. 1 that the planned location of the assembly (starting at a square adjacent to Parliament Avenue, following that avenue, and finishing in front of the Parliament building) was very important for the purpose of the assembly, since the demands that the participants intended to voice were related to and addressed to the Parliament.

On 28 August 2012, the Baku Administrative Economic Court No. 1 dismissed the applicants' complaint in application no. 69483/13, accepting the Baku City Executive Authority's (BCEA's) findings as valid reasons for refusing to authorise the assembly.

On 29 August 2012, the Baku Administrative Economic Court No. 1 dismissed the applicants' complaint in application no. 76319/13, accepting the Baku City Executive Authority's (BCEA's) findings as valid reasons for refusing to authorise the assembly.

On 17 April 2013, the Baku Administrative Economic Court No. 1 dismissed the applicant's complaint in application no. 30456/14, accepting the Baku City Executive Authority's (BCEA's) findings as valid reasons for refusing to authorise the assembly.
The applicants in all three applications appealed against the judgments of the Baku Administrative Economic Court No. 1, reiterating their previous complaints and arguments.
On 13 December 2012, the Baku Court of Appeal upheld the judgment of the Baku Administrative Economic Court No. 1 in application no. 69483/13, largely reiterating the first-instance court's findings.
On 20 December 2012, the Baku Court of Appeal upheld the judgment of the Baku Administrative Economic Court No. 1 in application no. 76319/13, largely reiterating the first-instance court's findings.
On 13 August 2013, the Baku Court of Appeal upheld the judgment of the Baku Administrative Economic Court No. 1 in application no. 30456/14, largely reiterating the first-instance court's findings.
On 13 March 2013, the Supreme Court of Azerbaijan upheld the judgment of the Baku Court of Appeal in application no. 69483/13, largely reiterating the appellate court's findings.
On 15 May 2013, the Supreme Court of Azerbaijan upheld the judgment of the Baku Court of Appeal in application no. 76319/13, largely reiterating the appellate court's findings.
On 20 November 2013, the Supreme Court of Azerbaijan upheld the judgment of the Baku Court of Appeal in application no. 30456/14, largely reiterating the appellate court's findings.

At the material time, Article 5 § I of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 required any person or persons organising an assembly listed in Article 3 of that Law to notify in advance the relevant body of the executive authority in written form, as a rule at least five days prior to the day of convening the intended assembly, for the purposes of authorising the assembly's time and place and the route of a march.

At the material time, Article 5 § I of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that submission of a notification in less than five days prior to the intended assembly must be justified by the organisers.
At the material time, Article 5 § II of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 required a written notification to include the form of the intended assembly.
At the material time, Article 5 § II of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 required a written notification to include the general purpose of the assembly.
At the material time, Article 5 § II of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 required a written notification to include the place and time of convening of the assembly.
At the material time, Article 5 § II of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 required a written notification to include the approximate number of participants.

At the material time, Article 5 § II of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 required a written notification to include, in respect of a march, its proposed route (the place where the march begins, its distance and an end location).

At the material time, Article 5 § II of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 required a written notification to include the name, surname, patronymic and address of the organisers of the assembly.
At the material time, Article 5 § II of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 required a written notification to include the date of submission of the written notification.

At the material time, Article 5 § II of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 required a written notification to include contact telephone numbers or, in the event of their absence, contact addresses.

At the material time, Article 5 § II of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that organisers may submit additional information before the relevant body of the executive authority makes a decision.
At the material time, Article 5 § III of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 required all organisers of the assembly to sign the written notification.
At the material time, Article 5 § IV of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that submission of a written notification for spontaneous assemblies is not required.

At the material time, Article 5 § IV of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that spontaneous assemblies may be restricted or stopped in accordance with the requirements specified in Articles 7 and 8 of that Law.

At the material time, Article 7 § I of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that no restrictions shall be placed on the right to freedom of assembly other than those that are prescribed by law and are necessary in a democratic society in the interests of national security or public safety, for the prevention of disorder or crime, for the protection of health or morals or for the protection of the rights and freedoms of others.

At the material time, Article 7 § II of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that restrictions on the freedom of assembly must be proportionate to the aim pursued and must not exceed necessary and sufficient limits.

At the material time, Article 7 § III of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that measures taken to restrict the freedom of assembly must be strictly necessary for achieving the aim which served as the reason for imposing the restriction.

At the material time, Article 7 § IV of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that freedom of assembly may be restricted in various ways including a change to the time and place of the assembly or a change to the route of a march, but only for the purposes prescribed under Article 7 § I of that Law.

At the material time, Article 8 § I of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that assemblies accompanied by calls for discrimination, discord (hostility), or violence, or incitement to national, racial or religious discord shall be prohibited.
At the material time, Article 8 § II of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that assemblies which promote war shall be prohibited.

At the material time, Article 8 § III of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that the holding of a peaceful assembly with political goals shall be prohibited twenty-four hours prior to the day and until closure of constituencies on the day of elections of the President of the Republic of Azerbaijan (on the entire State territory).

At the material time, Article 8 § III of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that the holding of a peaceful assembly with political goals shall be prohibited twenty-four hours prior to the day and until closure of constituencies on the day of elections of deputies to the Milli Mejlis (the Parliament) of the Republic of Azerbaijan (on the entire State territory).

At the material time, Article 8 § III of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that the holding of a peaceful assembly with political goals shall be prohibited twenty-four hours prior to the day and until closure of constituencies on the day of elections of deputies to the Ali Mejlis (the Parliament) of the Nakhichevan Autonomous Republic (on the territory of the Nakhichevan Autonomous Republic).

At the material time, Article 8 § III of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that the holding of a peaceful assembly with political goals shall be prohibited twenty-four hours prior to the day and until closure of constituencies on the day of municipal elections (on the territory of the respective city and district).

At the material time, Article 8 § III of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that the holding of a peaceful assembly with political goals shall be prohibited twenty-four hours prior to the day and until closure of constituencies on the day of a referendum.

At the material time, Article 8 § IV of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that on account of the need to implement security measures during international events of considerable State importance, the holding of peaceful assemblies with political goals on the eve of, and on the days of, those events may be prohibited by a decision of the relevant body of the executive authority, in accordance with the requirements prescribed under Article 7 of that Law.

At the material time, Article 8 § V of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that if necessary in a democratic society, an assembly may be prohibited by an order of the relevant body of the executive authority, in accordance with the requirements prescribed under Article 7 of that Law.

At the material time, Article 8 § VI of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that if necessary, an assembly may be stopped by an order of the relevant body of the executive authority, in accordance with the requirements prescribed under Article 7 of that Law.

At the material time, Article 8 § VII of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that prohibition or stopping of an assembly under Article 8 §§ IV, V and VI shall be considered as a measure of last resort and shall be applied only when the restrictions provided for under Article 7 of that Law are not sufficient.

At the material time, Article 8 § VIII of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that during a state of emergency, the holding of assemblies on the territory where that state of emergency is applied may be restricted or prohibited, in accordance with the requirements prescribed under the Law of the Republic of Azerbaijan on States of Emergency.

At the material time, Article 9 § I of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that any restriction on an intended place of a peaceful assembly shall be placed in accordance with the criteria determined under Article 7 of that Law.

At the material time, Article 9 § II of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that if another assembly has already been arranged at the place and time stipulated in a written notification submitted by the organisers of a counter-assembly and if there are sufficient grounds to conclude that a counter-assembly may cause a conflict between the parties, the relevant body of the executive authority shall propose to the organisers that they indicate a different place and time for the counter-assembly.

At the material time, Article 9 § II of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that a written notification of the amended time and place shall be submitted to the relevant body of the executive authority at least three days prior to the new date of an event.

At the material time, Article 9 § II of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that in the event that a counter-assembly is held, the police authorities shall take measures to ensure the security of the participants of both the assembly and the counter-assembly.

At the material time, Article 9 § III of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that the holding of gatherings, meetings, demonstrations and marches may be prohibited within a radius of 200 metres around the buildings of the Milli Madjlis (the Parliament) of Azerbaijan, the Presidential Palace, the official residence of the President of Azerbaijan, the Cabinet of Ministers, the Ali Madjlis of the Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic, the Cabinet of Ministers of the Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic, central, district and city executive authority bodies (the list of which shall be defined by the relevant executive authority), and the Constitutional Court of Azerbaijan, the Supreme Court, the appellate courts and the Supreme Court of the Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic.

At the material time, Article 9 § III of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that the holding of gatherings, meetings, demonstrations and marches may be prohibited on bridges, in tunnels, at construction sites, at production sites which present a danger to human life and health, and other sites requiring compliance with special technical norms for safety, specially protected nature areas and sites, protection zones of trunk pipelines, electrical networks with tension exceeding 1000 volts, airports, underground railways, railway facilities, defence facilities, technical facilities for water supply and sewerage systems, oil wells and waters.

At the material time, Article 9 § III of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that the holding of gatherings, meetings, demonstrations and marches may be prohibited in places allocated by the relevant body of the executive authority for holding special State events.

At the material time, Article 9 § III of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that the holding of gatherings, meetings, demonstrations and marches may be prohibited in areas used for military purposes and in places located closer than 150 metres to the boundaries of those areas, or, if necessary, within the security distance between those areas and participants of an assembly.

At the material time, Article 9 § III of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that the holding of gatherings, meetings, demonstrations and marches may be prohibited on the sites of penal facilities, pre-trial detention facilities, and psychiatric medical institutions, as well as in places located closer than 150 metres to the boundaries of those sites.

At the material time, Article 9 § IV of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that the holding of assemblies with political content in places of pilgrimage and worship, and in cemeteries, may be restricted.

At the material time, Article 9 § V of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that the number of picketers shall not exceed fifty persons, picketers shall not stand closer than ten metres to the entrance of a picketed location, shall not create obstacles for entry to and exit from the picketed location, and shall not use amplifiers above ten watts.

At the material time, Article 9 § VI of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that the relevant body of the executive authority shall allocate in each city and district special areas for conducting gatherings, meetings and demonstrations, and shall publish a list of those proposed places in the local press and bring it to the attention of the population by other means.
At the material time, Article 9 § VI of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that organisers may choose one of the places proposed for gatherings, meetings and demonstrations.

At the material time, Article 9 § VI of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that as a result of a petition, the relevant body of the executive authority may change the list of proposed places for gatherings, meetings and demonstrations.

At the material time, Article 9 § VII of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that the time for holding an assembly may be restricted by the relevant body of the executive authority, in accordance with the requirements of Article 7 of that Law.
